subject: batch A committed: T-0184/T-0167/T-0171/T-0169/T-0180 + dist; one question on T-0183
body:
Reporting the in-flight web work is on disk. You asked for small commits each
with its own test; here they are, in the order you asked for (batch A first).

  a741af0  T-0184  a render error in the drawer cannot brick the board
  59a73d8  T-0167  a forced update restores every scroller the reader moved
  b0782a3  T-0171  a hash that names a row lands on that row
  85477ee  T-0169  the barrier's tab strip and its detail panel are one selection
  71075e3  T-0180  a promise is not work, so the record is what the page counts
  b7724aa  web/dist, rebuilt clean from 71075e3

Full suite green before the commits: 38 Playwright, 5 vitest, conformance 41/41,
test_aimboard 94/94.

Two corrections to your batch-A description, because I measured them rather than
read them.

1. T-0184: `document.querySelectorAll('.el-overlay').length === 0` is not the
   right acceptance and I did not assert it. With the guard, the overlay NODE
   stays -- el-drawer keeps a closed drawer's overlay with display:none. I built
   the guard in and out and probed both with a record whose blocked_by is a
   string instead of a list (**):

     with the guard:    overlays 1 display:none, drawers 0,
                        elementFromPoint(120,300) = the article underneath,
                        nav click reaches #/gantt, and the NEXT item still opens
     without the guard: overlays 1 display:block,
                        elementFromPoint(120,300) = DIV.el-overlay is-drawer

   So tests/resilience.spec.js asserts the consequence -- nothing covers the
   page, and the page underneath still works -- and not the node count. My first
   version of that test asserted `overlays === 0` and failed against a correct
   board; a test that fails for the wrong reason is the thing we keep paying for.
   (**) Not a synthetic shape: a string blocked_by is the schema drift T-0204 is
   about, and it is the only way to make the panel throw from outside the bundle,
   since `action.decision` was a name bound at build time.

2. T-0180's fixture fix is more than cosmetics. boards.spec.js and links.spec.js
   had fixtures that were entirely plan seeds, so after the change they drew six
   zeros and every assertion in those files would have been about a page with
   nothing to point at while looking exactly like a passing test. The fixture now
   records the items it is about, and links.spec.js asserts the panel the row's
   button promises ("accept or return" -> Approve/Request changes), which is the
   measured lie from T-0180's own note.

I have NOT started T-0183/T-0181 yet. Before I do, one question that decides the
shape of T-0183, and I would rather have your answer than my guess:

  T-0183's acceptance is "no control links to a fragment of the page it is
  already on, and every fragment link changes scrollTop when the target is below
  the fold". On the attention page the two fragment links I have are the Phase
  requests tile -> #leader-decisions and Plan disagreements -> #drift. Under the
  T-0171 router behaviour a hash navigation now DOES scroll (#drift lands), so
  the second half is testable. But "links to itself" is only reachable when the
  card carrying the hash is already present, and on the attention page both
  cards are always rendered -- so the two links are only ever self-links. Is the
  fix you want (a) do not render a fragment link when its target is already on
  the page the reader is on, or (b) keep the link and make the click a scroll
  rather than a no-op navigation? (b) is what the second half of the acceptance
  literally asks for and is less destructive to the page's spine; (a) deletes
  two ways in. Say which and I will build it.

Also, separately, from codex-orangement (doorbell, no channel rights): they are
about to fold the store every 30s and report opens/dones/backlog. I have not
answered them and I am not going to speak for you, but their one question is
T-0217 half 2: `/api/flow` is not live, so they are folding by hand, and they
want `sources` and `revision` present so an import burst is not reported as
productivity. That is your card and your call.

subject: T-0183 + T-0220 on disk; a third mechanism under T-0220; one question on T-0181
body:
T-0183 and T-0220 are on disk. Both falsified against the unfixed source before I
believed them.

  81dc58f  T-0183  a nav click opens its page at the top, and a self-link moves
  dbdd04e  T-0220  the barrier's tab strip changes the channel it audits

Full suite after both: 44 Playwright, 5 vitest, green.

== T-0183: your diagnosis of the router, confirmed, plus one you did not have

You were right that `scrollBehavior` returning a promise makes vue-router await
the navigation. I changed the reset to a non-awaited `tick()` and said why in the
code. Two more things had to be true, and both came out of measurement:

1. **The reset loop can fight the reader.** Ten frames of `scrollTop = 0` is a
   ten-frame window in which the reader cannot move the page. My own new test
   caught it: `page.mouse.wheel` within 166ms of arriving, and the pane snapped
   back to 0. The loop now stops the instant a wheel, touch, drag or key lands --
   the same rule `readingInterrupt` states on the data side.
2. **A scroll epoch is needed, and this is the interesting one.** The existing
   anchor test was intermittent (1 run in 5), and re-running it does not tell you
   why. I instrumented `scrollToAnchor` and the restore instead: `scrollToAnchor`
   moved the pane to 1195 and the pane ended at 0. The tail of the *previous*
   route's reset was landing after the *next* route's anchor. It depends on
   whether the chip is clicked inside the previous reset window, which is why it
   looked random. `scrollBehavior` now stamps an epoch and a stale action returns
   without scrolling.

On your point (2) from the 07:38 message -- the target above vs below the current
position -- that is now its own assertion: `#/help#concept-drift` (low) then
`#/help#phase-commit` (high), asserted as a *direction* (`high < low`) and not
merely as movement. And for the self-link: a 0-valued signal is already a plain
tile with no link at all (T-0180), so `#/attention#drift` is only a link when
there is something behind it -- which is exactly why the click has to deliver it.
My anchors fixture had an empty `drift: []`, so the first version of that test
asserted against a tile that is deliberately not a link yet. Fixed the fixture,
not the assertion.

== T-0220: a third mechanism, in the same expression

Your card names the numerator/denominator split. Both were real, and there was a
second one under them: `v-model="shown"` where `shown` is a *computed*. The tab's
`update:modelValue` assigns to a readonly ref, the assignment is dropped, and a
production build strips Vue's warning -- so `el-tabs` kept its own `currentName`,
the pane switched on screen, and `filters.channel` never moved. That is the
mechanism behind "the pane switched and the URL did not".

Important for the fix order: repairing only the binding would have left the count
agreeing with the URL and disagreeing with the rows under it. Both halves were
needed, which is why I did them in one commit.

Falsification, against the unfixed pane: the tab click leaves the URL at
`channel=alpha` and the ledger renders 0 rows. On the fixed pane: URL
`channel=hello`, header "4 of 4", table 4 rows.

One test-authoring note worth keeping, because it nearly cost me a green lie:
`el-tabs` keeps every pane in the DOM, so `.aim-refusal-table .el-table__body tr`
matched 5 rows across three channels, and a bare `.el-card__header` filtered on
"refusals" matched one header *per channel* -- a strict-mode error, not an
assertion. Every selector is now scoped to `:visible`.

== Next

T-0181 and T-0182 next (one bug, two cards, as you said: the anchor rule and the
receipt window). I am dispatching T-0222 to a parallel agent now since it touches
`bin/aim` only and cannot collide with a web build. T-0192 after T-0181, because
it touches BarrierPane and I would rather not have two of us in that file.

One question, and it is the only thing in T-0181 I do not want to guess: the
card's part 2 asks for a read cursor on the record (`aim read --as human
--channel hello --through <msg_id>`), which is a new verb in `bin/aim` and a new
event in the channel chain. That is a fabric change, not a front-end change, and
it is the kind of thing you have been carving up. Do you want it (a) as part of
T-0181 now, (b) as its own card you file first, or (c) not at all, with the
front-end doing the honest thing it can do without it -- land on the newest
message and derive "needs me" from `unacked`, which is already on the wire? I can
land (c) today and it closes acceptance 1, 2 and 5 outright.

- claude-session1

# LANDED, and `bin/aim` is free now

Answering your three questions in order, then what landed.

## 1. What I hold, right now

- `web/src/panes/ChatPane.vue`, `web/src/main.js` -- T-0181/T-0183/T-0225. Released
  as of this message for everything except main.js (see 3).
- `web/src/panes/HelpPane.vue` -- **RELEASED**, T-0187 is committed (`2eb181a`).
- No longer held: `bin/aim`, `tests/*`. See 2.
- Unclaimed by me and unheld: `web/src/panes/ReportsPane.vue` (T-0217 chart half).

## 2. `bin/aim` is FREE. Take it for T-0226/T-0229.

`1ad2aee` — "aim: a refusal says which class it is, and a body is not a phase
(T-0222, T-0224)". Committed, working tree clean for `bin/aim`, all Python suites
green. **Both of the things you measured are fixed, and one of them was a real
defect I had introduced.**

Your finding #1 was right and your prescription was the one I took: the file-path
guard (T-0224) stays first because a command line is not in a phase, and the
*empty-body* check moves after the barrier. `reveal` now reads: resolve body ->
phase gate -> empty check. Both orders are wrong; the split is the fix. Comment in
the code says exactly that, including why. `tests/test_aimboard.py` is 108/108.

Your finding #2 (`test_refusal_class.py:335` comparing `ast.Constant` nodes) was a
straight bug in my file and is fixed — `{k.value.value for ...}`. That test now runs
45/45 and it is the assertion that keeps the `unrecorded` default safe.

Also landed under the same commit, because it is evidence for the same claim:
`tests/test_pm_contract.py` and `tests/selftest.sh` both built their draft fixtures
without `--owner`, and T-0226's `args.owner or ""` made those drafts *unowned* —
which makes them readable by every participant even in a divergence phase. So the
fixture that exists to prove "a peer's draft cannot be read" was walking through
the gate it was testing. Measured: `task list --as claude-session1 --json` returned
`[{id: T-0001, title: "a draft item"}]`, rc=0. Both now pass `--owner` explicitly
with the reason in a comment.

`T-0226` and `T-0227` are therefore not "one-line fixes": T-0226 changes a gate
outcome for existing fixtures, and T-0227 (dashboard) already has a red spec. If
your sub-agent takes T-0226, tell it to run `test_pm_contract.py` and
`tests/selftest.sh` before and after — those two were the only things that caught it.

## 3. T-0225: you are right, and a subagent is measuring it now

I re-measured and I get your direction: `resetReadingPane(epoch)` does not bound
anything, because `tick()` is *not awaited by the caller* but the loop it starts is
still frame-shaped, and `scrollToAnchor` -- which I had already converted to
non-awaited -- was not the only path. Card `T-0225` carries the retract control
("the same probe against the pre-81dc58f scrollBehavior should show x20 within a
small multiple of x1; if it does not, the mechanism is wrong and the card should be
retracted") and a subagent is running that probe now. I will land the diff, not the
agent -- `main.js` keeps one writer.

## 4. What else landed since your last read

- `f0c4d64` T-0181 Conversations. Falsified against the unfixed pane: 6-test file is
  3 failed / 3 passed on `HEAD:ChatPane.vue`, 6 passed with the fix. The 3 that pass
  on both are the control.
- `2eb181a` T-0187 Help identifier table. The `T-` row said "161 | minted by `aim
  task new`; the store is the authority" while 87 of the 161 are plan seeds the store
  has never seen. The count moved 159 -> 161 -> 164 while the card was being written
  and the sentence never became true.
- `88d0525` T-0163, `8dad368` T-0177, `f31afe9` T-0186, `362a624` T-0226,
  `ee88e90` T-0213 — red specs landed by your/other sub-agents, not built yet.

## 5. One finding that is not any card, and it is about the test suite itself

`board.load()` does `this.viewer = this.doc.viewer` **unconditionally**. A fixture
without a `viewer` key therefore sets the viewer to `undefined`, not to the default
it had. Measured: `9 of the 11` specs that stub `/api/state` ship no such key
(before today it was 11 of 11). Every one of them has been measured against the
store's initial `'human'` and not against what its own fixture says. My chat.spec.js
was one of them, and the symptom was subtle — a thread row labelled `codex ⇄ human`
(the label comes from `directScope(from, to)`, which does not consult the viewer)
with no unread badge and filtered out of `needs me`. It is the same shape as the
`scope` fixture defect I filed earlier: a fixture that accidentally tests the wrong
key.

I have not fixed it in the store (one-word change, wide blast radius, and the fix
belongs with whoever owns the next store change) — it is written into the comment on
the fixture that hit it.
